title: render()/render_and_wait() return type change silently breaks truthiness callers
description: dazpy/_render.py:320 - render()/render_and_wait() changed from returning bool (master) to returning a plain RenderOutcome dataclass with no __bool__. Any caller written as 'if rs.render():' (matching the old bool contract, and this is a public SDK method other projects like vangard-daz-mcp depend on) now always evaluates truthy, even when RenderOutcome(success=False, ...) is returned, silently treating failed renders as successful.
acceptance_criteria: Either add __bool__ to RenderOutcome that reflects success, or add a deprecation-safe path so existing truthiness checks behave correctly; document the breaking change in CHANGELOG.md.
close_reason: Added RenderOutcome.__bool__ reflecting success, documented the breaking change in CHANGELOG.md, and added regression tests for truthiness checks.

title: capture() throws ReferenceError on prevBg when backdrop_color is set
description: dazpy/_viewport.py:221 - DazViewport.capture()'s finish_script references the JS variable prevBg, but prevBg is only declared inside the separate prepare_script execute() call (a different HTTP round trip / JS scope). set_bg/restore_bg_js were written for the old single-script version and never had prevBg threaded through the prev_state dict the way selectionName/axesOn etc. were.
acceptance_criteria: capture(path, backdrop_color=(r,g,b)) succeeds (hide_overlays True and False) and restores the original viewport background without throwing.
close_reason: Fixed prevBg round-tripping through prev_state/prep_result JSON instead of a JS var across the two execute() calls; added regression tests for both hide_overlays branches.

title: Async render request stuck at 'running' forever on render failure (GH #34)
description: AsyncRequestManager has no watchdog/timeout that fails a stale 'running' render request. If the render never signals completion (blocked behind DAZ Studio's modal error dialog), GET /requests/:id stays 'running' indefinitely with no way for a client to detect failure short of a very long wait. Add either: (a) a render-error signal handler that resolves the request as 'failed' with the error message, or (b) a timeout that marks it failed after a bound. Depends on daz-script-server-3l5o to correctly detect the failure condition. (GH issue #34, suggestion #2)
acceptance_criteria: A render that errors resolves the async request to 'failed' (with a useful error message) within a bounded time, instead of staying 'running' indefinitely.

title: Render busy state never clears on failed/error render (GH #34)
description: SceneEventBroker only wires enterBusy()/exitBusy() to aboutToRender/renderFinished (SceneEventBroker.cpp:114-116). When a render errors, DAZ Studio pops a blocking modal and renderFinished never fires, so exitBusy() is never called and the plugin's busy counter stays stuck. Every subsequent /execute then returns 503 forever, recoverable only by restarting DAZ Studio. This is the root cause and the highest-leverage fix (GH issue #34, suggestion #1).
acceptance_criteria: A render that ends in error/abort no longer leaves the plugin permanently busy; /execute succeeds again without restarting DAZ Studio. exitBusy() fires on every render termination path, not just the success path.
notes:
Live-verified on running DAZ Studio 4 instance (2026-08-14): submitted an async render to a nonexistent drive (A:/...) via /render. Render itself succeeded (Iray converged to 97%), but the file-save step failed and DAZ Studio popped a blocking 'Error Saving' modal (Try Again / Choose New File / Cancel). While the modal was up, /execute correctly fail-fast'd with 503 STUDIO_BUSY (not a hang) and /health stayed responsive. After clicking Cancel on the modal, /execute immediately returned 200 and the async request transitioned running -> completed -- no DAZ Studio restart needed. Confirms DzRenderMgr::renderFinished(bool) fires as the guaranteed exit signal even on this non-happy-path outcome.

Also live-verified on DAZ Studio 6 (2026-08-14) with the identical procedure (nonexistent-drive output_path -> render succeeds, save fails, 'Error Saving' modal blocks main thread -> /execute correctly 503s STUDIO_BUSY while blocked, not hung -> after clicking Cancel, /execute immediately 200s and request transitions running -> completed). Confirms the fix holds across both SDK4 and SDK6 builds.

Note: this save-failure trick reproduces the same class of bug as the GH issue (a non-happy-path render outcome that pops a blocking modal), not the exact Iray-engine-failure repro (Scene.setBackdrop(null) -> Iray DB transaction abort). Attempted that exact repro separately on both DS4 and DS6 -- it hard-crashed both, with two DIFFERENT ACCESS_VIOLATION signatures (DzBackdrop::isVisible() on DS4, DzStyledTimeAsFramesPropertyWgt::~DzStyledTimeAsFramesPropertyWgt() on DS6), confirming Scene.setBackdrop(null) is a distinct, pre-existing DAZ Studio bug unrelated to this plugin and unsafe to use for live testing (see memory feedback_dazscript_blocking_dialogs). The save-failure repro is the safe, repeatable way to exercise this exact code path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Live-verify dazpy.lighting _look_at_euler yaw sign against real DAZ Studio
description:
Final whole-branch review of daz-script-server-p1af's ThreePointLightSetup work found that _look_at_euler's yaw formula in dazpy/lighting.py is likely sign-inverted for off-axis lights (nonzero X component in the aim direction -- this includes the default rig's key and fill lights, only the rim light at azimuth=180 is unaffected). Independently re-derived via dazpy/math3.py's own _euler_to_quat XYZ rotation convention (documented to match DAZ's bone-rotation channels): the correct formula is yaw = atan2(-direction.x, -direction.z), not the current atan2(direction.x, -direction.z). This derivation is solid but has NOT been empirically confirmed against a live DAZ Studio session, because no server was reachable during review (generic node rotation-control composition order was assumed to match the bone convention, but not independently confirmed for DzSpotLight/DzDistantLight/DzPointLight). Per user decision, the sign flip was deliberately withheld pending live verification rather than applied blind.

Action: with DAZ Studio running, create a rig via apply_three_point_light_setup at a known azimuth (e.g. 90) against a known target, then call DazLight.direction() on the resulting light and confirm it points at the target. If direction() confirms the current code's -90 deg is wrong and +90 is correct, apply the one-line fix (dazpy/lighting.py, the yaw calculation in _look_at_euler) and update test_look_at_euler_yaws_toward_90_azimuth_offset's expected value from -90.0 to +90.0 in tests/test_dazpy.py. If the live check instead confirms the current sign is correct, remove the caveat docstring note and close this without a code change.
close_reason: Confirmed live against running DAZ Studio: distant light rotated to y=+90 reports DazLight.direction()=(-1,0,~0), matching the intended convention; prior y=-90 was inverted. Fix applied and committed to feature/dazpy-lighting (commit f26e571). Full suite 557/557 passing.

title: Reintroduce face-region pass for LoRA-intensity control (no identity conditioning)
description:
Live-tuning against jason_a/abby_b (daz-script-server-r5br) found a new artifact after 3os's rebuild: the Graphic_Novel style LoRA at full strength (0.8) draws harsh 'pencil mark' ink lines on facial features (brow ridge, under-eye, under-nose) that read as artifactual rather than stylistic, confirmed by isolating lora_strength=0.0 (marks vanish entirely) vs 0.8 (marks present) with all ControlNet/composite settings held constant -- ruled out Canny threshold, composite opacity, and controlnet_lineart_weight as causes first (all had negligible effect). Lowering lora_strength globally (tested 0.3-0.6) fixes the face but also strips most of the body's ink-hatching texture, since the current architecture (post-3os) is a single full-image pass -- there's no way to apply a different LoRA intensity to the face vs body.

Root cause: faces read 'harsher' than bodies at any single style intensity (high-frequency geometric detail vs. smooth clothing), the same tension that originally motivated the FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID branch this epic's rebuild (3os) removed. That removal correctly fixed toe's specific artifacts (traced to IPAdapterFaceID/SEGSDetailer's identity-conditioning behavior at denoise=0.35/faceid_weight=1.0), but didn't address the underlying face/body intensity mismatch -- it just removed the only mechanism that let the two differ.

Fix: reintroduce a face-region crop+resample pass, reusing the parts of the old mechanism that were never implicated in toe (face bbox/SAM detection via UltralyticsDetectorProvider+SAMDetectorCombined, and the per-region ControlNet chain via ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS -- both confirmed innocent by toe's zero-baseline test, which disabled the whole face-refinement chain and still reproduced the artifacts). Explicitly exclude IPAdapterFaceID/IPAdapterInsightFaceLoader/IPAdapterUnifiedLoaderFaceID entirely -- no identity conditioning of any kind. New mechanism: a second LoraLoader patched at a lower strength than the main pass, feeding SEGSDetailer for the face crop resample, so face and body get independently tunable LoRA intensity.
design:
workflow_controlnet.json: add back UltralyticsDetectorProvider, BboxDetectorSEGS, SAMLoader, SAMDetectorCombined, MaskToSEGS, 3x ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS (normal/depth/lineart), SEGSDetailer, SEGSPaste -- same node shapes as the pre-3os workflow (see git show 04b6274~1:docs/examples/rendering/sprite_matrix/workflow_controlnet.json for reference), but with a NEW second LoraLoader node (patched at face_pass_lora_strength) feeding SEGSDetailer's basic_pipe instead of IPAdapterFaceID's output. No IPAdapter/InsightFace nodes at all.

New config.py fields on ComfyUIStageConfig: face_pass_enabled (bool), face_pass_lora_strength (float), face_pass_denoise (float), face_pass_guide_size (float), face_pass_bbox_dilation (int), face_pass_controlnet_normal_weight/depth_weight/lineart_weight (float) -- reuse the old face_detailer_* naming pattern minus faceid_weight (no identity conditioning to tune). Thread through schema.py, render_shot.py CLI, stylize_stage.py, workflow_builder.py following the same pattern as the removed face_detailer_* fields.

Live-tune face_pass_lora_strength against jason_a and abby_b once wired up -- 0.5 looked promising in ad-hoc testing during r5br but wasn't tested through the actual crop/paste mechanism, only as a global override.
acceptance_criteria: Face renders without harsh pencil-mark lines (brow ridge, under-eye, under-nose) on both jason_a and abby_b. Body retains full ink-hatching texture (main pass LoRA strength unchanged from whatever was chosen for body). No identity-conditioning artifacts reintroduced (toe stays fixed) -- verify since this does bring back SEGSDetailer, which was part of the original toe-implicated chain even though the root cause was specifically IPAdapterFaceID/faceid conditioning, not SEGSDetailer itself.
close_reason: Abandoned in favor of a simpler fix. Root cause was correctly diagnosed (Graphic_Novel LoRA draws harsh ink lines on facial creases at full strength) but the proposed face-region-pass fix backfired when tested: reusing the old per-region ControlNet weights (1.4/1.1/0.9, tuned for a different context with identity-locked low stylization) fought against the new lower-strength face LoRA and produced worse artifacts (heavy dark under-eye blocking), unresponsive to further LoRA reduction. Superseded by daz-script-server-r5br's negative-prompt suppression fix, which resolves the same root cause with zero architecture change. workflow_controlnet.json/workflow_builder.py changes from this issue were reverted.

title: Live-tune lineart_composite_opacity and validate toe/a5o resolved
description: Part of daz-script-server-3os. Once the rebuild is wired up (daz-script-server-7f2, -4a0, -5do, -pxmn), live-test against abby_b and jason_a: confirm daz-script-server-toe's artifacts (pale/ghostlike skin, harsh eye-shadow split) are gone; confirm facial identity is still recognizable without IPAdapterFaceID conditioning (the accepted trade-off of this rebuild); confirm daz-script-server-a5o (hair color drift) is resolved as a side effect; tune lineart_composite_opacity if full-strength (1.0) reads as over-inked/noisy on skin. Close toe and a5o once confirmed, or reopen/adjust design if identity loss is unacceptable.
acceptance_criteria: Live-verified against both abby_b and jason_a. Final lineart_composite_opacity value chosen and recorded in config.py comments. toe and a5o closed with reference to this validation, or a documented follow-up filed if identity conditioning needs to be reintroduced some other way.
notes: CORRECTION after initial close: 120/240 Canny thresholds still left small isolated stray marks (forehead, eyebrow tip, under-lip) on jason_a, visible at high zoom -- caught by user review of the copied final images. Isolated the residual cause (now that the LoRA's own line-drawing was already suppressed): tiny high-contrast points in the Iray render (specular highlights, skin pores) still exceeding even 120/240 in isolated spots. Tested 150/300, 200/400, and bilateral-filter pre-smoothing against a clean (negative-prompt-fixed) baseline -- all three cleared the residual marks equally well, so picked 150/300 as the more conservative change with no bilateral-filter complexity needed. Final default is 150/300, not 120/240. Re-verified through the actual production CLI (render_shot.py) at 3x zoom on both jason_a and abby_b -- clean.
close_reason:
Final fix has two parts, both live-verified against jason_a and abby_b through the actual production pipeline (render_shot.py):
1. Negative-prompt suppression (config.py ComfyUIStageConfig.negative_prompt): added terms against harsh facial crosshatching/under-eye ink/exaggerated brow lines. Root cause: the Graphic_Novel LoRA at full strength (0.8) draws ink strokes along facial creases as a learned stylistic behavior (confirmed via isolating lora_strength=0.0 vs 0.8 with all else held constant) -- promptable away without any architecture change or LoRA/body-hatching tradeoff.
2. Canny threshold retune (canvas_convert.derive_lineart default 80/160 -> 120/240, now also exposed as config/CLI knobs -- see daz-script-server-017n): removes the residual contribution from real Iray shading-edge lines (brow ridge, under-nose) picked up by the deterministic lineart composite pass, independent of the LoRA behavior.
Both were needed together -- prompt suppression alone left a faint under-nose/brow line from the composite step; threshold retune alone (tested earlier) didn't fully clear the LoRA-drawn lines.
lineart_composite_opacity stays at 1.0 (no longer needs lowering now that both upstream sources are addressed).
A face-region-pass approach (daz-script-server-fsq8) was attempted and abandoned -- see that issue's close reason.

title: Rebuild face stylization as line-color-split composite (replace FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID)
description: Root-cause work on daz-script-server-toe traced the pale/ghostlike-skin and harsh-shadow artifacts to the IPAdapterFaceID face-identity pass itself (denoise=0.35, faceid_weight=1.0), confirmed via a live zero-baseline test with the per-region ControlNet chain fully disabled (artifacts persisted). Rather than continue tuning that node's knobs, replace the two-pass architecture (main KSampler + SEGSDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID face refinement) with a single full-image KSampler pass followed by a deterministic post-process composite: multiply-blend the existing Canny lineart (canvas_convert.py derive_lineart(), already used as a ControlNet guide) over the color output. This decouples linework fidelity from diffusion sampling entirely, so neither pass's artifacts can desync face/body style. Design discussed and approved 2026-08-06 (no separate spec doc; captured here in bd).
design: Architecture: DAZ beauty render -> Canny lineart (unchanged derive_lineart) + Normal/Depth -> ComfyUI [LoRA + 3x ControlNetApply + KSampler + VAEDecode] -> stylize_stage.py multiply_blend(color, lineart_png, opacity) -> final output. Remove FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID chain entirely (nodes 60,62,64-75 in workflow_controlnet.json): UltralyticsDetectorProvider, BboxDetectorSEGS, SAMLoader/SAMDetectorCombined, MaskToSEGS, 3x ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS, IPAdapterInsightFaceLoader/IPAdapterUnifiedLoaderFaceID/IPAdapterFaceID, SEGSDetailer, SEGSPaste. SaveImage now saves the composited result. New config.py knob: lineart_composite_opacity (float, default 1.0). Removed config knobs: face_detailer_enabled/denoise/guide_size/bbox_dilation/faceid_weight/controlnet_normal_weight/controlnet_depth_weight/controlnet_lineart_weight. Trade-off accepted: no explicit facial-identity conditioning after this change -- likeness depends entirely on main pass's low denoise (0.35) + ControlNet; must be live-verified, not just assumed.
acceptance_criteria: Both toe artifacts (pale/ghostlike skin, harsh eye-shadow split) gone on abby_b and jason_a. Facial identity still recognizable without IPAdapterFaceID conditioning. daz-script-server-a5o (hair color drift) confirmed resolved as a side effect. lineart_composite_opacity tuned to a value that doesn't read as over-inked/noisy on flat skin regions.

title: Fix background box artifact in face-identity pass via SAM silhouette masking
description: Live testing showed a rectangular 'box' artifact behind the head/shoulders in stylized output: bbox_dilation=100 (added to fix the hair-color seam) pulled surrounding black background into the face-detailer crop region, which SEGSDetailer then subtly re-stylized (measured: background outside the crop stayed ~[5,4,4] pure black, inside the crop rose to ~[37,40,54] with high noise). Root cause: face_yolov8m.pt is bbox-only (confirmed via Impact-Subpack source -- SEGM_DETECTOR output is a NO_SEGM_DETECTOR() stub for bbox-only models), so BboxDetectorSEGS's noise mask is always a plain dilated rectangle, not a silhouette -- dilating enough to cover the hair inherently also covers surrounding background. Fixed by refining that rectangular hint into an actual head/hair silhouette via SAM (SAMLoader + SAMDetectorCombined with bbox_expansion=80/dilation=60 + MaskToSEGS with bbox_fill=false) before the crop-source swap. Verified live via precise pixel sampling: background pixels immediately outside the hair silhouette are pure black in every direction, while hair color remains correctly identity-preserved throughout (no regression of the earlier seam fix). title: DPB: zip extraction hardening for plugin installs
description: Harden the drag-and-drop plugin zip installer against path traversal (zip-slip), symlink entries, and zip-bomb resource exhaustion, since archives are effectively untrusted input dropped by the user. Originally flagged as a spec gap with no defenses specified.
design: Vendor miniz (single-header, MIT) matching the project existing cpp-httplib vendoring style -- no QuaZip or libarchive. Enforce max total uncompressed size, max entry count, and per-entry compression-ratio caps, checked live during decompression, not just trusted from header fields, so a crafted archive cannot lie about its size. Extract to a staging dir, validate manifest.json there, and only atomically rename into the final plugin dir once fully validated -- the live plugins dir never contains a partially-extracted or rejected archive. Note: this defends the filesystem, not against a malicious plugin actual Python code -- arbitrary code execution is inherent to running a third-party plugin and is a separate trust-model concern for community distribution, not solved by extraction hardening.
acceptance_criteria: Archives with path-traversal entries, symlink entries, or oversized/bomb content are rejected before or during extraction with no writes outside the staging dir; valid archives land atomically in the final plugin dir.

title: Investigate DzScript::hasInclude() heap corruption crash on script.reset()
description:
While running the full tests.py api suite (72 tests) against a live DAZ Studio 4 instance, the app crashed with ACCESS_VIOLATION in ntdll!RtlFreeHeap, called via MSVCR100.dll!free <- dzcore.dll!DzScript::hasInclude <- dzcore.dll!DzScript::~DzScript <- DazScriptServer.dll!DzScriptServerPane::handleExecuteRequest (script.reset() at DzScriptServerPane.cpp:1509).

This is a heap-corruption AV inside dzcore.dll's own DzScript destructor, freeing via the OLD Qt4-bundled CRT (MSVCR100). Matches the documented CRT-heap-mismatch bug class already known in this project (see memory: never store std::string from toStdString() in DazScriptServer structures). The triggering code path (handleExecuteRequest's SDK4 execute()/result() logic) is unchanged from before this session's SDK6 work - likely a pre-existing latent bug, never triggered before because nobody ran this thorough an automated stress test against a live instance.

Need to:
1. Bisect which specific test/script triggers it (heap corruption AVs often manifest later than the actual corrupting call, so the trigger may not be the test immediately preceding the crash).
2. Determine if this reproduces on DAZ Studio 6 (SDK6) too, or is SDK4/dzcore-version-specific.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED. Via live cdb debugging (sxe -c "kb;..." bpe breakpoint-exception filter, since dzcore's RtlReportCriticalFailure delivers a raw int3, not a structured 0xc0000374 SEH exception), captured two distinct heap-corruption stack traces in dzcore.dll, both triggered by completely normal DzScript usage:
1) Fresh-DzScript-per-request pattern: corrupts in dzcore!DzScript::hasInclude <- ~DzScript (called via our script.reset()/destructor).
2) Switched to a persistent/reused DzScript instance (setReuseInterpreter(true)) to avoid #1 -> corruption MOVED to dzcore!DzScriptContext::setArgs <- DzScript::doExecute <- DzScript::execute(args), triggered by repeatedly calling execute(args) on the same reused context.
FIX: keep the persistent/reused DzScript instance (avoids #1), AND avoid execute(args) entirely by injecting args via a getArguments() JS shim (same technique already used for SDK6, where execute(args)+result() never worked at all) then calling the no-arg execute() (avoids #2, since the no-arg path never touches DzScriptContext::setArgs).
VERIFIED: 6 consecutive full 72-test runs (432 total executions) against live DS4 with cdb attached and monitoring for breakpoint exceptions - zero crashes, zero heap-corruption events captured (previously crashed reliably within 1-2 runs). Also lazily construct the persistent DzScript (on first request) rather than in the pane constructor, since eager construction at pane-construction time (which runs very early during DAZ Studio's own startup/pane-restoration) caused a separate immediate startup crash.
Both dzcore.dll bugs (hasInclude/~DzScript and DzScriptContext::setArgs) are real, reproducible, closed-source bugs in DAZ Studio 4's dzcore.dll - confirmed they exist on v2.5.0 too (same dzcore.dll, unrelated to our SDK6 session's code changes), but our specific USAGE PATTERN (constructing per-request scripts, or passing args via execute(args)) is what exercises them. Worth reporting to Daz3D with this exact reproduction info if there's a support channel.
close_reason: Root-caused two distinct dzcore.dll heap-corruption bugs via live debugging; fixed by combining persistent/reused DzScript (lazily constructed) with a getArguments() JS shim to avoid DzScriptContext::setArgs entirely. Verified stable across 6 consecutive full 72-test runs with debugger monitoring confirming zero corruption events.

title: Add POST /render endpoint (single render, async)
description:
VN production workflows need to trigger DAZ renders programmatically. Without a render endpoint, every render requires manual GUI interaction, making batch sprite production impossible to automate.

Implement POST /render that accepts a render job, enqueues it through the existing AsyncRequestManager, executes on the main thread, and returns a request_id immediately.

Request body schema:
- output_path (required, absolute path)
- width / height (optional, override scene render settings)
- format: png|jpg|tiff|exr (optional, inferred from output_path extension)
- camera (optional, null = active camera)
- engine (optional, null = scene default: iray|3delight|filament)
- figure / morphs (optional, single-figure morph dict)
- figures (optional, list of {name, morphs} for multi-figure scenes)
- iray_samples (optional quality override)

Render jobs use id prefix 'rnd-' and flow through the existing processNextAsyncRequest() path as a special request type. The server generates a DazScript snippet from the morph dict, applies morphs via findPropertyByLabel(), then calls App.getRenderMgr().render(opts). Unknown morph names are silently skipped (non-fatal). Status/result polling via existing /requests/:id/status and /requests/:id/result endpoints.

Open questions to resolve during implementation:
1. morph reset between variants (reset_morphs flag needed?)
2. Figure lookup fallback: error vs fall back to primary figure
3. Add isRender flag to AsyncRequest struct in AsyncRequestManager.h
design:
1. reset_morphs flag: Add reset_morphs: bool to POST /render request body. When true, reset all figure morphs to zero on the main thread before applying the morphs dict and rendering. Required for correct variant rendering when the same figure is reused across batch jobs.

2. Figure lookup failure = error: On figure lookup failure, return an HTTP error (not a silent fallback). Before any render step begins, run a validation pass over the entire figures array to identify all figure references and validate they resolve to scene nodes. This surfaces all bad references at once rather than failing mid-render.

3. RequestType enum instead of isRender bool: Add RequestType enum (REQUEST_TYPE_SCRIPT, REQUEST_TYPE_RENDER) to AsyncRequest struct rather than a boolean isRender flag. Thread it through submit() or a new submitRender() overload. Used in two places: (a) cancelJson() — only invoke killRenderOnMainThread() when cancelling a render request, not any running request; (b) processNextAsyncRequest() — gate render-progress signal wiring for future SSE progress endpoint (owd).

title: SceneSaving busy detection never fires for some save paths
description:
Live testing on feature/studio-busy-handling (through commit 720736f) found that saving to a specific file (2 separate test runs) never fired scene.saving/scene.saved SSE events at all -- confirmed via a live SSE stream capture during the save (push-based, so absence is conclusive, not a timing/polling miss). This means SceneEventBroker::onSceneSaveStarting()/onSceneSaved() are never invoked for this save path, so the SceneSaving busy-tracking branch (enterBusy(MainThreadBusy::SceneSaving)) is currently a no-op for at least this trigger. DzProgress::isActive()/DzBackgroundProgress::isActive() also did not catch a blocking window in either test.

Contrast with scene load (fires reliably, just has a separate trailing-tail gap after sceneLoaded -- see daz-script-server-063) and render (fires cleanly with zero gaps -- aboutToRender/renderFinished bracket the whole operation).

Practical impact is likely smaller than the load case since saves observed were fast (~2s each), but it's a real gap, not just an edge case: any request landing during a save currently has no fast-fail coverage at all, same as pre-fix behavior, for however long the save takes.

Needs investigation: why doesn't DzScene::sceneSaveStarting()/sceneSaved() fire for 'save to a specific file'? Possible causes: this save path may route through a different internal DAZ Studio API than DzScene::saveFile() (e.g. asset/content manager save, or a script-driven save vs UI Save/Save As), or the signal semantics may differ from what was assumed when this feature was designed. Should test other save triggers (Ctrl+S, File > Save, File > Save As with different destinations) to see if any of them do fire the signals, to isolate which specific trigger path is unbracketed.

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling-design.md. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling.md.
close_reason: Root cause found via code inspection + live test: /scene/save-copy has two branches. The dirty-scene branch calls dzScene->saveScene() and DOES fire sceneSaveStarting/sceneSaved reliably -- confirmed live via a concurrent SSE capture during a real save-copy call against the currently-open (dirty) scene, both the destPath save and the origFilename restore-save fired cleanly. The clean-scene fast path (QFile::copy, src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp ~2931) never calls saveScene() at all, so signals never fire for it -- this fully explains '2/2 test runs never fired', since repeated test runs against an already-saved scene would deterministically hit this branch every time, not flakily. Fixed by making SceneEventBroker::enterBusy()/exitBusy() public and wrapping handleSaveCopy()'s entire body (both branches) in an RAII BusyScope guard, so busy tracking for this handler no longer depends on DzScene's internal signal coverage. Verified: builds cleanly (link step blocked only by the DLL being locked by the currently-running Studio instance -- expected, install requires Studio closed). title: DPB: token authentication reusing existing SecureRandom
description: Secure the daemon port 18812 endpoints with a token, matching the existing DSS auth model on port 18811, without reimplementing token generation or crypto in Python.
design: DSS remains the sole token generator: reuse AuthenticationService and SecureRandom generateHexToken exactly as done for the existing dazscriptserver_token.txt, writing to a new dazpythonbridge_token.txt under the same daz3d dir with the same chmod-600 enforcement and warning. The Python daemon only ever reads this file at its own startup via an X-DPB-Token header check -- it never generates or rotates a token itself. Single source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: DPB daemon rejects requests without a valid X-DPB-Token; token file is generated by DSS existing SecureRandom-backed code path, not by any Python-side crypto.

title: DPB: plugin status/management UI and daemon API
description: Non-modal plugin status pane in DSS showing each installed plugin state, resolving, ready, starting, running, failed, or disabled, with start, stop, restart, enable, and disable controls, so users have visibility into background installs and worker health without anything blocking the UI.
design: Daemon exposes GET /plugins, returning state, pid, memory, last-used, and POST /plugins/ID/start, stop, restart, enable, disable. DSS polls via QTimer using async QNetworkAccessManager calls, never a blocking call on the Qt main thread, consistent with the existing AsyncRequestManager polling pattern already used for async DazScript requests. A plugin in resolving or disabled state rejects calls to its exposed_functions with a distinct DazPluginNotReadyError rather than a raw connection failure.
acceptance_criteria: Status pane reflects install progress, running, idle, and failed state, and responds to manual start, stop, restart, enable, disable without freezing the DAZ Studio UI at any point.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copies are daz-python-bridge-sop.6/.8 (closed).

title: DPB: warm worker process lifecycle and crash policy
description: Each plugin isolated venv needs its own live Python process to actually execute calls, since a venv is not a process. Spawn a persistent warm worker subprocess per plugin lazily on first call, not eagerly, and not spawn-per-call which would pay interpreter startup latency on every invocation.
design: Worker spawned on first /execute call routed to that plugin_id, using that plugin own venv interpreter, communicating over a local pipe or loopback socket. Idle-timeout eviction, for example 10 minutes unused, reclaims memory. Crash policy: one automatic restart on worker crash; if it crashes again, flip to failed state and require manual restart via the status UI -- unlimited silent auto-restart would crash-loop a systematically broken plugin invisibly.
acceptance_criteria: First call to a plugin has a visible but bounded cold start; repeated calls are fast with no re-spawn; an idle plugin worker is reaped after timeout and respawns transparently on next call; a worker that crashes twice in a row ends in failed state, not a restart loop.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copy is daz-python-bridge-sop.5 (closed).

title: DPB: per-plugin venv isolation and eager dependency resolution
description: Each installed plugin gets its own venv instead of a shared site-packages, so two plugins pinning conflicting dependency versions do not clobber each other. Dependencies are resolved eagerly at install time, right after the zip is committed, not lazily on first call, so a broken requirements.txt surfaces immediately in the plugin status pane instead of on first invocation.
design: uv venv for the plugin dir, then uv pip install -r requirements.txt scoped to that venv. Reuses the Python 3.11 build already downloaded during bootstrap so per-plugin venv creation is sub-second. Disk cost stays low across many plugins because uv global package cache is content-addressable and hardlinks shared packages such as numpy across venvs rather than duplicating them. This replaces the original spec single shared venv with a --target install approach.
acceptance_criteria: Two plugins with conflicting dependency versions install and run without interfering; a plugin with an unresolvable requirements.txt fails at install time, status failed, rather than at first call.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copy is daz-python-bridge-sop.4 (closed).

title: DPB: /run inline Python execution endpoint + scripting pane

Add a DSS UI pane, Script-IDE style, where users type Python and click Execute.
design: run_venv stays fully isolated -- it must NOT import already-installed plugin packages, keeping it a clean-slate scratch environment like DAZ Studio own Script IDE.

title: DPB: daemon bootstrap and JIT venv setup
description: First-run JIT bootstrap for the DPB daemon: download platform uv binary, install Python 3.11 via uv, create the isolated run_venv (used only by the /run inline-scripting endpoint, not by plugins), and launch the FastAPI daemon bound to 127.0.0.1:18812. Everything else in the DPB epic depends on this daemon existing and being launchable/health-checkable from DSS.
design: Layout: AppData/Daz 3D/Studio4/DazPythonBridge/bin/uv, run_venv/, plugins/ID/venv/. Per-plugin venvs are created lazily elsewhere, NOT at bootstrap time -- bootstrap only creates run_venv/. DSS must be able to detect daemon liveness and know if the daemon process died so the plugin status UI can reflect it.

title: Daz Python Bridge (DPB): bidirectional Python plugin ecosystem
description: Add a Python daemon (port 18812) that DazScript can call into synchronously, plus a drag-and-drop plugin installer, so DazScript-driven workflows can invoke Python (numpy/ML/HTTP clients) inline and the community can distribute installable Python add-ons for DSS. Complements the existing dazpy client (Python calling INTO DAZ via port 18811) with the reverse direction (DAZ calling INTO Python). Full design worked out gap-by-gap in conversation before implementation; see child issues for the resolved architecture per gap.
design: Two ports: 18811 (existing, DAZ-as-server) unchanged. 18812 (new) is a FastAPI daemon DSS launches. Two venv kinds: an isolated run_venv/ for the inline /run scripting pane (Script-IDE analogue), and one isolated venv per installed plugin under plugins/<id>/venv/ (solves shared-site-packages dependency conflicts). Each plugin gets a lazily-spawned warm worker subprocess (not spawn-per-call) with idle-timeout eviction and a one-shot auto-restart-then-fail-loud crash policy. Zip installs are hardened (miniz, path-traversal/symlink rejection, live-enforced size caps, stage-then-commit atomic install) and dependency-resolved eagerly at install time so failures surface immediately in a non-modal plugin status pane (states: resolving/ready/starting/running/failed/disabled) with start/stop/restart/enable/disable controls. DSS's outbound calls to the daemon use QNetworkAccessManager (async) + QTimer polling, never blocking the Qt main thread. Token auth reuses the existing SecureRandom/AuthenticationService C++ code (DSS generates+owns the token file, daemon only reads it) rather than reimplementing crypto in Python. Reinstall follows the existing script-registry convention (overwrite-by-id), sequenced as stop-worker -> stage-commit -> re-resolve-deps.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 originally-identified spec gaps have a resolved design reflected in child issues; child issues are implementable independently once their listed dependencies are closed.
close_reason: Epic for the duplicate issues closed above -- see daz-python-bridge-sop (closed) for the real history, and daz-script-server-5sw (closed) for what replaced it.

title: Iray Canvas: read/enable existing canvases and return per-canvas output paths
description:
Combined tier 1 + tier 2 of daz-script-server-llr (tier 2 folded in after research confirmed the same API covers both -- see superseded daz-script-server-dwy). GitHub issue #19: expose Iray Canvas enumeration, creation, and per-canvas output paths through dazpy.

Confirmed live-instance API (no C++ server changes needed -- pure DazScript via the existing /execute path, same pattern as the Iray quality-preset code in dazpy/_render.py):

  holder = App.getRenderMgr().getRenderElementObjects()[1]   // DzIrayPropertyHolder

  holder.renderToCanvases: bool                    // master on/off for canvas output
  holder.getNumCanvasDefinitions(): int
  holder.getCanvasDefinition(i): canvas
  holder.findCanvasDefinition(name, createIfMissing): canvas | null
  holder.removeCanvasDefinition(canvas)

  canvas.name: string                              // e.g. 'Canvas1', auto-generated but editable
  canvas.canvasType: int                           // enum -- Beauty=0, Diffuse=1, Specular=2, Glossy=3,
                                                    // Emission=4, LightGroup=5, EnvironmentLighting=6,
                                                    // LPE=7, Irradiance=8, Alpha=9, Shadow=10,
                                                    // AmbientOcclusion=11, Distance=12, Depth=13,
                                                    // MaterialTag=14, MaterialID=15, ObjectID=16,
                                                    // Normal=17, TextureCoordinate=18, BSDFWeight=19,
                                                    // ConvergenceHeatmap=20, PostToon=21, WorldPosition=22
  canvas.canvasTypeToString(int) / canvasTypeFromString(string)
  canvas.index: int

Output file convention (confirmed empirically against a live render): <output_dir>/<basename>_canvases/<basename>-<canvasName>-<canvasTypeString>.exr

renderToCanvases confirmed to actually gate output (folder present/absent both directions, re-tested twice). canvas.processingDisabled does NOT gate per-canvas output -- confirmed it does not skip render even when true; drop it from scope. UI widgets (Render Settings > Advanced > Canvases) do not auto-refresh after scripted property writes -- must call pane.refresh() on MainWindow.getPaneMgr().findPane('DzRenderSettingsPane') after any scripted write to keep the UI in sync; this should be standard practice in the implementation, not just ad hoc during testing.
acceptance_criteria: DazRenderSettings (dazpy/_render.py) gains: list_canvases() (name, type, index), add_canvas(name, canvas_type) using findCanvasDefinition(name, true) + set canvasType, remove_canvas(name), get/set renderToCanvases master toggle (calling pane.refresh() after the write), and a way to retrieve each canvas's resolved output path after a render (derived from the confirmed <basename>-<canvasName>-<canvasTypeString>.exr convention). Unit tests mock DazClient; integration tests scoped with -k against a live DAZ Studio instance per project convention.

title: Fix: changing server port doesn't stop the old listener thread
description: Discovered during DS6 testing: changing the port in the pane's Settings UI (e.g. 18811 -> 18812) without restarting DAZ Studio leaves the OLD listener thread/httplib::Server bound and serving requests in addition to the new one - both ports end up live simultaneously against the same DzScriptServerPane instance, served by a single process. This is a real bug in the start/stop/apply-settings logic (likely onStartClicked()/applySettings() needs to fully stop the previous ServerListenThread/httplib::Server before starting a new one on the new port), not just a testing artifact - confirmed by curl'ing both ports and getting live responses from both after a port change with no restart.
close_reason: Fixed: stopServer() was deleting the httplib::Server object before joining the listener thread, a use-after-free race; the freed memory could be reused by the next startServer() call, leaving both old and new listeners apparently live. Reordered to join/terminate the thread before deleting the Server object.

title: Main orchestrator script (main.py)
description:
Build the main.py entry point that wires together the viewport snapshot, file watcher, and ComfyUI submission into a single runnable workflow.

## Why
The individual components (viewport capture, file watcher, ComfyUI client) are usable independently, but the orchestrator is what makes this a working example. It should be runnable with a single command and show clear progress output.

## What needs to be done
- main.py CLI with argparse:
  - --config path to config file (optional, falls back to defaults)
  - --output path for the final enhanced image
  - --denoise override denoise strength
  - --no-watch skip file watcher, expect the snapshot path directly (--snapshot-path)
  - --dry-run print what would happen without executing
- Execution flow:
  1. Load config (merge CLI args)
  2. Connect dazpy client (DazClient), verify server health
  3. Connect ComfyUI client, verify /system_stats
  4. Set up file watcher on watch_dir
  5. Call DazViewport.capture(watch_dir/snapshot.png, width, height)
  6. Wait for watcher to return the file path
  7. Upload image to ComfyUI (client.upload_image)
  8. Build workflow from template (workflow_builder.build)
  9. Submit workflow (client.queue_prompt)
  10. Wait for result (client.wait_for_result) with progress dots
  11. Download and save output to --output path
  12. Print summary: input path, output path, duration
- Error handling: clear messages for server not running, file not found, timeout

## Design decisions
- Use --no-watch mode for development/testing when you already have a source image
- Always print the output path at the end so it can be piped or opened programmatically

## Acceptance criteria
- python main.py runs end-to-end with both servers running
- --dry-run prints plan without executing
- Error messages are human-readable (not stack traces) for the common failure cases

title: img2img ComfyUI workflow template (workflow.json)
description:
Create a ComfyUI workflow JSON template tuned for photorealistic enhancement of DAZ Studio viewport captures.

## Why
ComfyUI workflows are parameterized JSON graphs. The template must be designed for img2img enhancement — not text-to-image generation — with settings biased toward sharpness, detail retention, and photorealism rather than creative deviation.

## What needs to be done
- Create workflow.json as a standard ComfyUI API-format (prompt dict, not UI format)
- Nodes to include:
  1. CheckpointLoaderSimple — loads a photorealistic SDXL or SD1.5 checkpoint
  2. LoadImage — references the uploaded input image
  3. VAEEncode — encode input image to latent
  4. CLIPTextEncode (positive) — fixed prompt: 'photorealistic, sharp focus, high detail, 8k, professional photography, clean lighting'
  5. CLIPTextEncode (negative) — '(blurry, low quality, noise, artifact, watermark:1.4), painterly, cartoon, drawing'
  6. KSampler — denoise=0.45, steps=20, cfg=7.0, sampler=dpmpp_2m, scheduler=karras
  7. VAEDecode — decode back to pixel space
  8. SaveImage — writes to ComfyUI output folder
- Parameterize via Python string substitution for: checkpoint_name, denoise_strength, steps, positive_prompt override
- workflow_builder.py — Python module that loads the template and fills in parameters, returning a dict ready for queue_prompt()

## Design decisions
- denoise=0.45 as default: strong enough to improve quality, low enough to preserve scene composition and character positions
- Use DPM++ 2M Karras for quality/speed balance
- Keep positive prompt minimal and generic so it works across scene types without fighting the source content

## Acceptance criteria
- workflow_builder.build(image_ref, config) returns a valid ComfyUI prompt dict
- Can be loaded and submitted to a real ComfyUI instance without modification errors

title: File watcher module (file_watcher.py)
description:
Build a file watcher that monitors a directory for a new image file and triggers a callback when the file is fully written.

## Why
DAZ Studio's captureToFile() is fire-and-forget from the script side — it writes to disk but the dazpy client doesn't know the exact moment the file is ready. A file watcher decouples the capture trigger from the ComfyUI submission and handles the write-completion race condition reliably.

## What needs to be done
- FileWatcher class using the watchdog library:
  - watch(directory: str, callback: Callable[[str], None], pattern: str = '*.png', timeout: float = 30.0) -> str
  - Blocks until a matching file appears in the directory and is fully written
  - Write-completion detection: poll file size until it stops growing (100ms interval, 3 stable readings)
  - Returns the full path of the detected file
  - Raises TimeoutError if timeout elapses with no file
- Also support async-style: watch_async() that starts a background thread and calls callback when ready
- cleanup: remove the handler after first match (one-shot mode by default)

## Design decisions
- watchdog Observer is heavier than polling but handles network drives and non-inotify systems correctly on Windows
- One-shot mode is correct for this pipeline (one capture → one submission)
- Write-completion by size stability is more reliable than a fixed sleep

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit test: mock watchdog events, assert callback fires with correct path
- Integration test: write a file to a temp dir, assert watch() returns the path

title: ComfyUI HTTP API client module
description:
Build a self-contained ComfyUI client module (comfyui_client.py) that handles all HTTP communication with a local ComfyUI instance.

## Why
ComfyUI exposes a REST+WebSocket API that is not officially documented but is well understood from community usage. Encapsulating it in a client class keeps the orchestrator clean and makes the client independently testable.

## What needs to be done
- ComfyUIClient class with:
  - __init__(base_url='http://127.0.0.1:8188', client_id=None)
  - upload_image(path: str) -> str — POST /upload/image, returns 'subfolder/filename'
  - queue_prompt(workflow: dict) -> str — POST /prompt, returns prompt_id
  - get_history(prompt_id: str) -> dict — GET /history/{prompt_id}
  - wait_for_result(prompt_id: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict — polls get_history until outputs appear
  - download_image(filename: str, subfolder: str = '', folder_type: str = 'output') -> bytes — GET /view
  - save_result(prompt_id: str, output_path: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> str — combines wait + download + save
  - get_system_stats() -> dict — GET /system_stats (for health check)
- All methods raise ComfyUIError (custom exception) on non-2xx responses
- Polling in wait_for_result uses exponential backoff (0.5s → 2s max)

## Design decisions
- Use requests library not httpx (simpler, no async needed for this workflow)
- client_id is a UUID generated once per instance, used in prompt submissions
- No WebSocket — polling is sufficient for batch workflows

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests cover upload, queue, wait, download with mocked requests
- ComfyUIError raised correctly on HTTP errors
- save_result() produces a file on disk given a valid ComfyUI instance

title: Add POST /render/batch endpoint for variant rendering
description:
VN production requires rendering many variants of the same scene (expressions, poses) — often 10-30 per character setup. Submitting each individually requires many round trips and makes orchestration harder.

Implement POST /render/batch that accepts a base config plus a list of variants, enqueues each variant as an independent async render request, and returns all request_ids in one response.

Request schema:
  base: {camera, width, height, engine, figure} — shared settings
  variants: [{output_path, morphs, figures, ...overrides}] — per-render settings

Each variant is an independent AsyncRequest with isRender=true. Returns:
  {batch_id: 'bat-...', request_ids: [...], total: N}

Key design point: variants render sequentially (DAZ cannot render two scenes simultaneously), but the HTTP client can interleave other requests between polls. Document both usage patterns:
  Pattern A: submit full batch upfront, poll all request_ids
  Pattern B: submit one at a time, use setup between renders for complex scene changes

Atomicity: if variant N fails, variants N+1..M still render. Per-variant errors in results.
notes: Implemented. POST /render/batch accepts {base, variants:[]}. Base provides optional defaults (camera, width, height, engine, figure/figures, reset_morphs). Each variant requires output_path; merges with base for remaining fields. Figure merge: variant figures/figure wins; variant morphs+single base figure merges morphs (variant overrides). All variants validated and pre-flighted before any are enqueued (fail-fast). Enqueue failures mid-batch return 503 with partial count. Response: {batch_id:'bat-...', request_ids:[...], total:N}. Each rnd-id compatible with existing /requests/:id/status, /requests/:id/result, and GET /render/:id/progress endpoints. Max 100 variants per batch.

title: SSE endpoint GET /scene/events
description:
Add SSE handler in DzScriptServerPane.cpp (alongside existing handlers).

Route: GET /scene/events

Query params:
- filter= comma-separated list of categories: node,skeleton,light,camera,selection,scene,time,render
  Default (omitted): all categories enabled

Handler logic:
1. Check auth (reuse existing token validation)
2. Check IP whitelist (reuse existing check)
3. Parse ?filter= into bitmask
4. Set response headers: Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, Connection: keep-alive
5. Create SubscriberQueue, register with m_pEventBroker
6. Loop:
   a. pop(15000) -- 15s timeout
   b. If empty (timeout): write ':keepalive\n\n', flush -- client detects disconnect on failed flush
   c. If event: write 'data: <json>\n\n', flush
   d. If flush fails (client gone): break
7. Unregister SubscriberQueue from broker, delete queue

Note: httplib keeps the handler alive for the duration -- this is a long-running handler, same pattern as the existing long-poll result handler.

   Strategy: on timeChanging, start/restart a 150ms QTimer (single-shot)
   On timer fire: emit one time.changed event with current scene time
   On timeChanged() (manual scrub): emit immediately, cancel timer

2. nodeSelectionListChanged() -- can burst during multi-select
   Strategy: 50ms debounce, coalesce into single selection.list_changed

Implementation:

- QTimer* m_pSelectionDebounce (50ms, single-shot)

title: Bounded-wait backstop for the residual busy-detection race window
description:
Both signal-based (SceneEventBroker depth counter) and DzProgress/DzBackgroundProgress busy detection are now live on feature/studio-busy-handling (commit 720736f), and together catch the large majority of a scene load's busy window. Live testing (3 File->Open runs) found a residual gap: the trailing node-streaming phase after sceneLoaded() fires appears to run as several chained sub-operations, each apparently its own progress instance, with brief gaps between them where neither DzScene signals nor DzProgress::isActive()/DzBackgroundProgress::isActive() report busy. A request whose busy check runs during one of those gaps still commits to the blocking Qt::BlockingQueuedConnection call and waits out the remainder of that phase -- observed up to ~15s in testing, bounded by scene complexity, not indefinite like the pre-fix behavior, but still a real (if much smaller and rarer) block-then-succeed window instead of a clean fast 503.

Decision (2026-07-23, live testing session): ship the current two-signal detection as-is rather than close this fully now -- it's already a large improvement over the original unbounded hang. This issue tracks the deferred, more invasive fix: cap how long any HTTP thread can actually block on the main-thread invokeMethod call itself (independent of whether busy detection correctly predicted the state in advance), so even an undetected busy window can't hang past a bound. This was originally proposed as 'Approach 3' in the initial design brainstorming for this feature (bounded wait + fallback to async-style response) and revisited as a live option during testing.

Design note: the underlying BlockingQueuedConnection call can't be cancelled once queued -- a timeout on the calling side would leave an orphaned queued call that still executes on the main thread later, with its result discarded. Needs a decision on what the HTTP response contract looks like in that case (plain 503 retry, or auto-convert to the async-request-tracking flow so the result isn't lost). See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling-design.md for the original design and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling.md for the implementation plan this extends.
close_reason: Won't fix, after implementation review. The already-shipped pre-check busy detection (commit 720736f, on master) already turns the original unbounded hang into a bounded, self-correcting ~15s slow-but-correct response — no data loss, no wrong result, just latency. A working bounded-wait backstop was implemented and independently verified concurrency-correct (race-free CAS ceiling, sound thread/promise lifetimes, Qt6-portable), but final review surfaced a real behavioral hazard: on timeout the queued main-thread call is NOT cancelled (Qt has no API for this) and keeps running, so the 503 the client receives is misleading (the operation is still executing), and dazpy's retry_on_busy could re-run it — a double-execution risk strictly worse than the slow-but-correct wait it replaces. The default 20s timeout also exceeds the one measured gap (~15s), so it offers little value against the observed problem and is really speculative insurance against a worse, never-observed wedged-main-thread case. Decision: the tradeoff isn't worth it as scoped; keep the existing pre-check detection only. The implementation (branch feature/studio-busy-handling, commits 680b267..467ea7b) is not merged to master. Revisit only if a genuinely unbounded hang is observed in practice, with a design that avoids the discard-and-maybe-retry hazard (e.g. never reusing a retry-safe error code for a timeout that doesn't actually stop the underlying work).

title: Harden main-thread busy state with a depth counter if DAZ nests scene signals
description: SceneEventBroker's busy-state tracker (src/SceneEventBroker.cpp) uses a single scalar reset to Idle unconditionally in each *Finished/*Cleared/*Loaded/*Saved slot. If DAZ Studio ever nests scene-clear signals inside a scene-load (loadStarting -> clearStarting -> cleared -> ... -> loaded), onSceneCleared would reset busy to Idle while the load is still blocking the main thread, briefly reopening the indefinite-hang window. Flagged by final whole-branch review of feature/studio-busy-handling (commit 89aaafd). Gate this on what daz-script-server-fbk's manual smoke test observes -- only needed if nesting is actually confirmed. Fix: replace the scalar with a depth counter (increment on *Starting, decrement on *Finished, busy = count>0).
notes: Fix implemented on feature/studio-busy-handling commit 474244d (depth counter via enterBusy/exitBusy). Confirmed real via live testing under daz-script-server-fbk, not just hypothetical. Will close once fbk's re-test confirms the fix resolves the observed hang.

title: DS4 (Qt 4.8) cannot build for arm64: qatomic_powerpc.h asm constraint error
description: DAZStudio4.5+ SDK bundles Qt 4.8, which predates Apple Silicon and has no real arm64 atomics support. CI run 29248727943 confirmed: building DazScriptServer for arm64 against DS4/Qt4 fails at DAZStudio4.5+ SDK/include/QtCore/qatomic_powerpc.h:126 and :143 with 'error: invalid output constraint =&b in asm' — Qt4's platform detection falls back to a bogus PowerPC atomics path on arm64 rather than a real arm64 implementation. This was previously masked by the CMakeLists.txt CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES FORCE bug (fixed in master 43ca8ce), which silently built x86_64 even when arm64/universal was requested. Unlike the DS6 case (daz-script-server-250, missing arm64 SDK lib), this is a Qt4 SDK/toolchain limitation with no likely fix from DAZ; probably means DS4 macOS builds should stay x86_64-only for the foreseeable future. build-macos.yml's macos-arm-ds4 and macos-universal-ds4 legs are currently red until this is addressed (see also test-build.yml's build-macos-arm-ds4 job).
acceptance_criteria: Either DS4 arm64 compiles successfully, or build-macos.yml explicitly skips sdk-version=4 + arm64/universal with a clear message (matching the DS6 guard) instead of failing red
close_reason: Decision: DAZ Studio 6 itself is an x86_64 build running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon, so an x86_64-only plugin (DS4 or DS6) works fine there and native arm64 isn't actually required. We still build/publish 'Apple Silicon' named plugin artifacts for naming-consistency, but the build workflows stay as-is (force-compiling x86_64 for these legs). No further arm64 SDK/toolchain work needed.

This is a DAZ Studio 6 SDK limitation, not a repo config bug — the CMakeLists.txt CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES FORCE bug (fixed in daz-script-server master commit 43ca8ce) was masking this by silently building x86_64 even when arm64 was requested. build-macos.yml now explicitly skips the sdk-version=6 + arm64/universal combo with a clear CI summary message instead of failing red. This issue tracks getting an arm64 (or universal) libdzcore.dylib published to daz-studio-sdks so the DS6 Apple Silicon leg can actually build.

This issue remains open: the real fix (DAZ publishing a native arm64 libdzcore.dylib) hasn't happened; the acceptance criteria is unchanged.
close_reason: Decision: DAZ Studio 6 itself is an x86_64 build running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon, so an x86_64-only plugin (DS4 or DS6) works fine there and native arm64 isn't actually required. title: Fix sleeve/arm length: use 3D diagonal distance instead of Y-only
description: Sleeve length reports 35.7 cm on G9 base figure (expected ~58-62 cm). The _vertical_distance() helper measures only the Y-coordinate difference. Affects sleeve_length, and potentially front_waist_length and inseam when figure is not in T-pose. Verified live on Genesis 9 base figure 2026-06-18.

title: AxisRemap polish: docs, __eq__, dead state, _mat3_to_quat branch coverage
description:
Follow-up from the final review of daz-script-server-okpk (AxisRemap coordinate conversion, merged in af4bb11). Four Minor items were deferred rather than blocking merge:

1. docs/api/math3.rst and README.md's math3 blurb were never updated to mention AxisRemap/Y_UP_TO_Z_UP.
2. AxisRemap has no __eq__/__hash__ (Vec3 and Quat both do). If added, must add both together (eq without hash makes instances unhashable).
3. AxisRemap._matrix and _det are stored on the instance but never read after construction except via the _rotation_quat gate; harmless dead state, low priority.
4. dazpy/math3.py's _mat3_to_quat has 4 branches (trace>0 plus 3 diagonal-dominant cases); the shipped test suite in tests/test_math3.py only exercises the trace>0 branch. Two independent reviewers verified the other 3 branches correct out-of-band during review, but there's no regression test protecting them. A property-based test sweeping all 24 proper axis permutations (see the final review's suggested test) would close this permanently.

Also worth considering as a separate, larger follow-up (not part of this issue): an AxisRemap.inverse() method, since round-tripping currently requires hand-deriving the inverse remap by hand.
acceptance_criteria: All four items addressed or explicitly triaged as won't-fix with reasoning.
close_reason: Docs updated (README + math3.rst), AxisRemap gained __eq__/__hash__, removed dead _matrix/_det slots (kept as locals), added 24-permutation property test covering all _mat3_to_quat branches. inverse() deliberately left as separate future item per issue note.
